terms.meaning: A unit where 1 means one million US dollars.
A yearly exchange rate used to convert a figure from another currency into US dollars.
Converting many differently stored values into one common form.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Sets the budget unit rule
sections.what: The header states that every budget column is stored in US dollar millions, that non-US figures are held converted at their own year's rate, and that the reported currency is kept in a separate field.
sections.why: The header comment says it follows a Yard-wide normalisation done in 2026-10.
sections.watch_out: Code elsewhere must not assume a raw dollar figure, because the rule says no industry stores raw dollars.

sections.name: RAW_DOLLAR_INDUSTRIES
sections.title: Placeholder list for raw-dollar industries
sections.what: Holds a list of industries whose budget figures arrive in raw dollars. The list is empty, so no industry is treated that way right now.
sections.why: The code comment says it is kept empty so a future raw-dollar import has one place to declare itself.
sections.watch_out: The comment says any industry added here must also have its values normalized, so adding one without that step would give wrong budget figures.

sections.name: budgetToMillions
sections.title: Turn budget text into millions
sections.what: Converts a stored budget value into a plain number, in millions for industries that store full dollars, and refuses any text that is not a plain number.
sections.why: Likely reason: the code comment says stored budgets are plain numbers, so other text is refused rather than guessed.
sections.watch_out: The unit depends on the industry name matching the full-dollar set exactly, so a misspelled industry name gives a wrong amount.

summary: Sets the rule every budget figure in the app follows: stored in US dollar millions, with the source currency recorded separately.
purpose: Keeps all budget numbers in the same unit so totals and comparisons make sense.
why: The header comment says the rule was set by a Yard-wide normalisation, and that non-US figures are converted at a fixed annual rate.
how: Only the header comment is in this packet. The file's functions, RAW_DOLLAR_INDUSTRIES and budgetToMillions, are named in the outline but their code is not shown, so their steps are not described here.
inputs: Not visible in this packet beyond the budgetToMillions name, which portfolio.ts calls with a budget value and an industry.
risks: Industries listed as raw dollar industries may be handled differently. A wrong unit in one place would make totals wrong by a factor of one million.
debug: If a budget looks a million times too large or small, check the currency and unit recorded for that project, then the budgetToMillions helper and its industry list.
